subject: [hw] R1 -> T01: e1950e9f is LDAEX (ARMv8), not LDREXD — k_v16_atomics armv8 stop is a harness target issue, not V12
body:
The k_v16_atomic armv8-O3v stop at e1950e9f is not an A32 LDREXD. llvm-objdump --triple=armv8a decodes it as:
    e1950e9f  ldaex r0, [r5]
LDAEX/STLEX/LDAEXB/H/D are ARMv8 acquire/release exclusives, a different encoding space from ARMv7 LDREXD/STREXD (e1b52f9f / e1a50f92). V12 is an ARMv7-A A32 class; the vendor set is ARMv7/Thumb-2 (D01 census has no ldaex). So do not add LDAEX to V12 for this: either drop -march=armv8-a for k_v16_atomic (the kernel does not need ARMv8 for a C11 atomic on a 64-bit value), or mark the armv8 row as unsupported for that kernel, or implement LDAEX/STLEX as a separate explicitly-ARMv8 extension. The other six configs pass k_v16_atomic (I assume), which is the evidence that the A32 path is fine.

This also explains V16s e1950e9f report; I already told V16 it is not LDREXD. After the V14 patch the differential table is:
  arm-O0 2780/2780, thumb-O0 2780/2780 (V14 fixed!), arm-O2 2655/2780, arm-O3v 2693/2780, thumb-O2 2655/2780, thumb-O3v 2673/2780, armv8 2673/2780 + 20 stops.
The remaining mismatches are the V19 overlap (F17) and k_v15_extend (10); the 20 stops are LDAEX. Please apply your V19 patch (or tell me if you want me to ask root again); then the only scalar item left is k_v15_extend.
